citations.text: The 聽 entry’s historical sequence is labeled 商, 西周, 戰國, 說文小篆, 漢, then clerical forms. The author analyzes the oracle-bone and bronze forms as associative, with ear and mouth representing speech received by the ear, and describes the received Shuowen account as adding 悳 as a sound element. The continuation discusses extensions from hearing to accepting/obeying, inquiry/governance, and waiting. It then says 聽 is now simplified to 听, separately identified with the Shuowen 口-plus-斤 analysis and smiling sense. These are the author’s analyses; the scan does not establish every proposed historical relationship.

consulted_citations.text: The printed page gives yǐn on the 听 headword line and tīng beneath it. The paragraph assigns ‘smiling appearance’ and 口-plus-斤 phonosemantic analysis to the yǐn entry, then says 听 has been a simplified form of 聽 since the Yuan. The scan agrees with the corpus text and confirms printed page 84. It does not state that the historical sound analysis explains the simplified form’s adoption.
